message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether deleting my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch was the right thing to do. Let me start by going through the situation again to make sure I understand all the details. At the beginning of the school year, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help her parents. I brought my Switch because my school is more than an hour away, and I wanted something to do during the train commute. My stepbrother really wanted to play on it, and it actually helped distract him while I studied. So, I made a new profile for him so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That seemed like a good idea at the time because it kept things organized and prevented any accidental deletions or changes to my games. When I got back to school, I started getting annoyed because every time I wanted to play a game or go to the eShop, I had to click on my profile. It was a minor inconvenience, but it annoyed me enough that I just deleted his profile. I thought it was no big deal because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit, so he wouldn't have access to it anyway. But then, during Thanksgiving, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. My stepbrother picked it up to play and came into the kitchen where I was talking with my dad. He started freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it, he started crying, not full-on crying, but his eyes were watery and red. Now he's holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knew my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn't think it was a big deal since I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit. So, the question is: Was it right or wrong for me to delete my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch? Let me break this down. First, I made the profile to help him and to keep my saves safe. That was considerate. But then, when I got annoyed with the minor inconvenience of switching profiles, I deleted it without considering how it might affect him. He was using it, enjoying it, and when it was gone, he was upset. I think about ownership. The Switch is mine, so technically, I can do what I want with it. But when I let someone else use it, especially a younger sibling, I have a responsibility to consider their feelings and experiences. Deleting his profile without warning or discussing it first was probably hurtful. Also, my dad's reaction was that it was mean. That's a parent's perspective, but it makes sense because it's about empathy and understanding the impact of my actions on others. Even though I didn't think it was a big deal, it was significant enough to my stepbrother that it caused him emotional distress. I should have communicated with him before deleting the profile. Maybe I could have found another solution, like setting up parental controls or just being more patient with the minor inconvenience. Deleting it without any discussion was abrupt and unfair. In the end, while I have the right to manage my own device, I also have a responsibility to be kind and considerate, especially towards family members. My action, while not malicious, still caused harm, and that's something I should take into account.
